title: Relative sheaf descente on a prescribed Noetherian envelope
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $B\to A$ any homomorphism of commutative rings, and $p:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ a separated finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Write $Y_A=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}B}\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Fix a closed immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow Y_A$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] pseudo-coherent relative to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]. For every integer $a$, there exist a finite type $B$-algebra $B'$ which is Noetherian, a factorization $B\to B'\to A$, a closed immersion $k:Z\hookrightarrow Y_{B'}$, a closed immersion $j':X\hookrightarrow Z_A$ with $k_Aj'=j$, and $F\in D(\mathcal O_Z)$ with bounded coherent cohomology [pqf-def-coherent], together with a morphism $\gamma:F\to Ru_*E$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image], where $q:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}B'$ is the structure morphism and $u:X\to Z$ is $j'$ followed by projection. Put $M=\widetilde A[0]$ on $\operatorname{Spec}B'$ and $T=Lq^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}F$ [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Define $\theta:T\to Ru_*E$ by derived adjunction [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint]: its transpose is the composite
$$Lu^*T\simeq L(q\circ u)^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lu^*F
 \longrightarrow \mathcal O_X\otimes^{\mathbf L}E\simeq E,$$
using the scalar action $L(q\circ u)^*\widetilde A\to\mathcal O_X$ from the given $A$-structure on $X$, and the transpose $Lu^*F\to E$ of $\gamma$. Then the cone $C$ of $\theta$ has quasi-coherent cohomology and $H^i(C)=0$ for every $i\ge a$. Neither $B\to A$ nor $B'\to A$ is assumed flat, and $j'$ need not be an isomorphism. This is an approximation of sheaves on $Z$ before taking any global sections; the envelope $Y/B$ is prescribed.

proof.text: Set $K=Rj_*E$ on $Y_A$. A closed immersion is affine, so affine derived pushforward sends $E$ to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{Y_A})$. Both $X$ and $Y_A$ are locally of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}A$: on an affine chart the closed immersion is a quotient map of rings and hence is finite type. For every integer $m$, closed-support invariance transfers relative $m$-pseudo-coherence from $E$ to $K$. Thus $K$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

proof.text: Use the proposition $\mathcal P(W)$ defined in the two-open-locality lemma. We prove it for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq Y$ by induction on the size of a finite affine cover; the quantification over every finite coefficient stage $D$ is retained throughout the induction. For the empty open every derived object is zero, so take $D'=D$, $F=0$, $\gamma=0$. This gives the empty-cover base without any nonzero-ring hypothesis.

proof.text: We will use the affine pushforward dictionary. For a ring map $R_0\to R_1$ and an $R_1$-module $N$, the sections of $f_*\widetilde N$ on $D(r)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ are $N_{r}$, by the formula for associated sheaves. Thus $f_*\widetilde N=\widetilde{\operatorname{Res}N}$ naturally, including on maps. For an unbounded module complex use this equality termwise. The affine pushforward resolution lemma says that pushing a quasi-coherent-term complex into a K-injective resolution is a quasi-isomorphism; consequently $Rf_*\widetilde N^\bullet\simeq\widetilde{\operatorname{Res}N^\bullet}$ in the derived category, naturally. We use this for polynomial embeddings and for coefficient projections. No flatness is needed.

proof.text: For the one-affine-open case write $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Its ring $R$ is finite type over $B$. Fix the $D,K,a$ quantified by $\mathcal P(W)$, and put $S=R\otimes_B D$, so $W_D=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $W_A=\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_D A)$. The affine equivalence represents $K$ by an $(S\otimes_D A)$-module complex. Choose a polynomial presentation $D[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\twoheadrightarrow S$, and base change it to $A$. The all-affine-charts criterion shows that the pushforward of $K$ along the corresponding closed polynomial embedding is $m$-pseudo-coherent for every $m$; hence it is pseudo-coherent. The affine pseudo-coherence criterion says precisely that the underlying $A[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$-complex is pseudo-coherent. Apply the affine coefficient-window lift with base $D$ and algebra $S$ to obtain $D'$, $L$ and $\gamma$. Its Noetherian-base hypothesis holds because $D$ is finite type over the Noetherian ring $B$.

source.place: Agent assembly of the sheaf descente prerequisite for the unnumbered Kiehl assertion after Tag 0CSD; primary source WANTED. Supporting affine and gluing sources are specified in report.md.

proof.text: Sheafify $L$ on $W_{D'}=\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_D D')$ and call it $F$. This ring is Noetherian, so the finitely generated cohomology modules of $L$ give coherent cohomology sheaves of $F$, zero outside the same finite interval. Affine pushforward identifies the sheafified $\gamma$ with $F\to R\pi_*K$. The affine pullback formula and the affine tilde-tensor comparison (clause (3) of the cited affine derived-tensor lemma, $\widetilde{M^\bullet}\otimes^{\mathbf L}\widetilde{N^\bullet}\cong\widetilde{M^\bullet\otimes^{\mathbf L}N^\bullet}$ on an affine scheme) identify the source of $\theta$ with the sheaf associated to $A\otimes_{D'}^{\mathbf L}L$: on resolutions the cancellation is $(S'\otimes_{D'}^{\mathbf L}A)\otimes_{S'}^{\mathbf L}L\simeq A\otimes_{D'}^{\mathbf L}L$, where $S'=S\otimes_D D'$. Under adjunction its map to $R\pi_*K$ is $1\otimes\gamma$ followed by the $A$-action, since the transpose sends a scalar and a section to that scalar times the transpose of $\gamma$. Thus this is exactly the affine lift's map, not an underived base-change map. The exact affine equivalence preserves its cone and cohomology. This proves $\mathcal P(W)$.

proof.text: For the induction step, suppose $W=W_1\cup\cdots\cup W_n$ with the $W_i$ affine and $n>1$. Put $U=W_1\cup\cdots\cup W_{n-1}$ and $V=W_n$. By induction $\mathcal P(U)$ holds, and the affine case gives $\mathcal P(V)$. Separatedness over the affine base implies each $W_i\cap W_n$ is affine. Therefore $U\cap V$ is covered by at most $n-1$ affines, and the same induction gives $\mathcal P(U\cap V)$. These opens are quasi-compact by their finite affine covers. Apply two-open locality to obtain $\mathcal P(W)$. Finally $Y$ has a finite affine cover since it is finite type over an affine scheme. Thus $\mathcal P(Y)$ holds, including for empty $Y$.

proof.text: Apply $\mathcal P(Y)$ with the initial coefficient stage $D=B$, the complex $K=Rj_*E$ from step 1, and the required integer $a$. Write $B'=D'$ for the resulting finite type algebra. It is Noetherian by finite-type permanence. Set $Z=Y_{B'}$, $k=\mathrm{id}_{Y_{B'}}$, and $j'=j$ under $Z_A=Y_A$. The identity is a closed immersion, $j'$ is the given closed immersion, and $k_Aj'=j$. Let $\pi:Y_A\to Y_{B'}$ be projection and $u=\pi j$. The canonical composition isomorphism identifies $R\pi_*K$ with $Ru_*E$; transport $\gamma$ through it. The produced $F$ has the required bounded coherent cohomology on $Z$.

proof.text: The scalar action used in $\mathcal P(Y)$ is the given $A$-action on $Y_A$. After the composition identification, its transpose to $X$ is obtained by applying $Lj^*$ to the transpose on $Y_A$ and then the counit $Lj^*Rj_*E\to E$. Pullback composition identifies the scalar factor with $L(q\circ u)^*\widetilde A$. The counit is $A$-linear, so this transpose is the scalar action tensored with the transpose of the transported $\gamma$, exactly the formula defining $\theta$ in the item. Adjunction therefore identifies the two maps. Their cones are isomorphic; the cone supplied by $\mathcal P(Y)$ is quasi-coherent and has $H^i=0$ for every $i\geq a$. This is a bound on sheaves on $Z$; no global sections or flat base change are used.
